summary: We developed an AI-powered agricultural intelligence and crop diagnostics platform that transforms complex NASA Earth observation data into actionable, farmer-friendly insights. Our system integrates multi-year satellite time-series data from NASA MODIS (vegetation vitality via NDVI) and NASA POWER (root-zone and surface soil moisture, soil surface temperature, and extreme weather metrics) with computer vision models for early plant disease detection and smart farming calendars.   To address the challenge of making space-grade data accessible to local farmers and agronomists, we engineered a Land Health & Desertification Tracker. By analyzing temporal trends across vegetation vitality, thermal stress, and hydrological balance, our platform detects early signs of soil degradation, salinization, and drought risk—visualizing them through an intuitive traffic-light health chart and automated agronomic recommendations.This project is vital because climate volatility, water scarcity, and soil degradation directly threaten global food security. Empowering farmers with proactive, data-driven diagnostics bridges the gap between orbital science and field-level sustainability, protecting crop yields and preserving arable land.
details:
Our platform is a comprehensive, AI-powered agricultural expert system that acts as a digital agronomist for farmers and landowners. By simply inputting a farm's geographic coordinates (Latitude and Longitude) or uploading a crop image, the system executes a multi-stage diagnostic pipeline:

  1. Multi-Year Land Health & Desertification Tracking: The backend automatically queries orbital data from NASA MODIS (MOD13Q1 for 250m 16-day Normalized Difference Vegetation Index - NDVI) and NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (GWETROOT for root-zone soil moisture, GWETTOP for surface soil moisture, TS for soil surface temperature, and PRECTOTCORR for precipitation). Using linear regression trend analysis (np.polyfit), it calculates the historical trajectory of the land, generating a unified Land Health & Desertification Risk Score.
  2. Automated Agronomic Diagnostics: By cross-referencing vegetation vitality slopes with root-zone moisture and thermal stress trends, the system distinguishes between water-scarcity drought (declining NDVI + declining moisture + rising soil temperature) and soil salinization/chemical degradation (declining NDVI despite adequate root-zone moisture).
  3. Computer Vision Disease Detection (disease_predictor.py): Farmers can upload leaf images to a deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) module to identify plant diseases at early stages and receive targeted treatment protocols.
    image_5a9805.jpg
  4. Extreme Weather Alerts & Smart Farming Calendar (extreme_weather.py & farming_calendar.py): The platform monitors micro-climatic anomalies (heatwaves, frost, or heavy rain) and provides localized, crop-specific scheduling for irrigation, fertilization, and harvesting.
    image_5a9805.jpg

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Empowering Non-Technical Farmers: Satellite remote sensing is traditionally locked behind complex scientific formats (HDF5/NetCDF) and specialized GIS software. Our platform translates these raw orbital metrics into a visual "Traffic-Light" Health Chart (Green = Healthy Zone, Yellow = Moderate Stress, Red = Drought/Salinity Risk) and plain-language Arabic/English actionable advice.
  • Proactive Resource Optimization: Farmers can detect root-zone water deficits and soil degradation months before irreversible crop failure occurs, optimizing irrigation water usage and preventing over-fertilization.
  • Intended Impact: Supporting sustainable agriculture in arid and semi-arid regions (such as Egypt's Nile Delta and reclaimed desert lands), combating desertification, reducing crop losses, and strengthening local food security against climate change.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Programming Languages: Python (Backend, Data Science, Deep Learning), JavaScript/HTML/CSS (Frontend Web Interface).
    image_5a9805.jpg
  • NASA APIs & Datasets: NASA ORNL DAAC MODIS Web Service REST API (MOD13Q1) and NASA POWER Agroclimatology REST API.
    image_5a9805.jpg
  • AI, Data Science & Visualization Libraries: PyTorch / Deep Learning frameworks (for CNN plant disease classification), Pandas & NumPy (for time-series resampling, alignment, and linear regression trend modeling), Requests (for asynchronous/chunked REST API data retrieval), and Matplotlib (for server-side Base64 visual chart generation).
    image_5a9805.jpg
  • Backend & Web Architecture: FastAPI / Flask RESTful APIs (main.py, core_service.py) serving JSON payloads and Base64-encoded diagnostic plots.
    image_5a9805.jpg
  • Development Environment & Hardware: Developed on Ubuntu Linux using Visual Studio Code, Conda virtual environments (torch_env), Git/GitHub, and accelerated via an NVIDIA Quadro GPU setup.
    image_5a9805.jpg

How Our Project Is Creative

  • Multi-Dimensional Diagnostic Matrix: Rather than displaying isolated satellite numbers like raw NDVI, our system creatively fuses biological vitality (MODIS NDVI) with hydrological and thermal physics (NASA POWER root moisture & soil temperature). If a farm's greenery drops while root moisture remains high, the system creatively deduces potential soil salinity or nutrient lock-up rather than simple drought.
  • Farmer-Centric Visual Storytelling: Instead of overwhelming users with dual-axis scientific plots, we engineered a single, intuitive 0–100% Land Health Score overlaid on color-coded risk zones, allowing any educated farmer to understand a 3-year satellite history in under 3 seconds.
  • Resilient Hybrid Architecture: To overcome satellite API rate limits (such as MODIS 10-date chunk restrictions) and potential cloud-cover gaps, we built an automated chunking pipeline paired with a hydrological fallback estimator, ensuring 100% uptime and real-time responsiveness.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  1. Accessibility & Cognitive Load: How do we make NASA data useful to a farmer standing in a field? Every technical metric was paired with a direct, actionable agricultural recommendation (e.g., mulching, soil leaching for salinity, or organic compost application).
  2. Local Environmental Context: Designing the thresholds specifically around the agricultural realities of arid/semi-arid climates and river deltas, where surface evaporation is high and soil salinization is a silent threat.
  3. API Reliability & Speed: Ensuring fast response times by aggregating daily and 16-day satellite records into aligned monthly time-series (resample("ME")) and encoding charts directly into lightweight Base64 streams for seamless web rendering.
